hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive static gain): higher heater power produces higher steady-state temperature.
Step response has observable lag/first-order delay with time constant of tens of seconds, not instantaneous.
No large dead-zone: even moderate u around 0.3-0.5 produces a measurable rise above ambient.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.2 or below due to heat loss to the room.
Response is approximately linear across input levels: doubling u approximately doubles steady-state rise above ambient.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is in the mid-range around 0.4-0.6.
Sensor noise on y is small (<~0.01) so trends and end-slope in measured_summary are interpretable.

uncertainty: Estimates first-order gain magnitude and lag from a mid-level hold, which is required to choose any steady-state feedforward and feedback timing for control.
expected: If positive-gain with self-cooling hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.21 toward ~0.4-0.55 with visible lag, slope decreasing over the hold; end slope indicates whether equilibrium is reached.
safety_argument: Starting at y=0.2052, worst-case bound is 0.2052+0.006*0.5*180=0.7452 which stays below the 0.85 soft limit with margin, so supervisor will accept it and hard cutoff at 0.9 will not be approached.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive static gain): higher heater power produces higher steady-state temperature.
Step response has observable lag with dead-time ~15-40s and dominant time constant ~130-180s, not instantaneous.
No large dead-zone: even moderate u around 0.3-0.5 produces a measurable rise above ambient.

Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.32: u=0.3 settles at 0.469 with zero slope and u=0.34 settles at 0.526 with ~0 slope, bracketing the band.
Sensor noise on y is small (~0.005-0.01) so trends and end-slope in measured_summary are interpretable.

operator_note: Heater brackets target with 0.3 holding low at 0.469 and 0.34 holding high at 0.526, so ~0.32 should hold 0.5 and controller design can proceed.

justification: 5 settled/transient holds resolve all control-critical uncertainties: direction (H1 certain positive), dead-time/tau (H2 ~20-40s/130-180s from E1-E3 lags and E2 cooling and E4/E6 settling), no dead-zone (H3), self-cooling to ~0.2 (H4 from E2 decay with negative slope), feedforward bracketed to ~0.32 within 0.02 (H6 from E4 settled 0.469 and E6 settled 0.526), noise small (H7). Remaining tau/ambient/linearity errors are small and correctable by conservative PI with integral around 0.32 feedforward, acceptable for 300s settling evaluation.
